text:
alex: Heads-up — noticed a privilege escalation vector in the GPU pool onboarding flow. A CI job still has cluster-admin via a ClusterRoleBinding tied to `ci-deploy-sa`.

mira: omg — where did that come from? I thought we scoped that to ns:infra last quarter.

alex: It was supposed to be scoped but the rollout PR reverted yesterday (1743f6c) and CI reverted the change when running the legacy pipeline. I ran `kubectl get clusterrolebinding ci-deploy-binding -o yaml` and it pointed at the serviceAccount `infra/ci-deploy-sa`.

jordan: Can you paste the binding? we should remove cluster-admin and create a namespaced Role with just `deployments, pods/exec` for the deploy flow.

alex: pasted snippet:

```yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: ci-deploy-binding
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: ci-deploy-sa
  namespace: infra
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: cluster-admin
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
```

sam: yikes. That's the one that grants access to node-level stuff — so anyone with CI creds could affect GPU node labels or taints and sneak workload schedules.

mira: Action plan: (1) pin CI to use namespaced RoleBinding instead of ClusterRoleBinding, (2) create minimal Role `deploy-runner` in infra that allows only `create/update` on deployments and `get/list` on pods, (3) rotate CI tokens / serviceaccount secrets, (4) enable audit log for these SA tokens. Agree?

jordan: +1. Also audit current RoleBindings referencing `infra/ci-deploy-sa` cluster-wide. Quick command:

```
kubectl get clusterrolebinding -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.subjects[]? | select(.name=="ci-deploy-sa"))'
```

ops-bot: Incident 2026-04-04T12:45:20Z — automated check detected a ClusterRoleBinding to cluster-admin for infra:ci-deploy-sa. Created ticket SECURITY-488.

alex: I created a hotfix branch `rbac/gpu-min-priv` and a PR with replacement RoleBinding. PR link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rbcs/PR-892

mira: For KMS: we also rely on CI to unwrap artifacts with KMS key `projects/redwood/keys/ci-artifacts`. If we rotate SA tokens we need to ensure the new SA still has kms.decrypt via IAM binding. Do we want to move to workload identity to reduce long-lived secrets?

jordan: yes — workload identity would be best. Short term: rotate SA token and update KMS IAM to allow the new SA. Long term: migrate to workload identity and add a GCP KMS key policy that references the SA federated identity.

sam: Also, consider adding an admission controller policy to prevent creating ClusterRoleBindings except via an approved PR label. That would stop future accidental reverts.

alex: Agreed. Two fast safety controls: restrict `kubectl create clusterrolebinding` via OPA Gatekeeper constraint to a whitelist of admin SAs, and block cluster-admin roleRef for non-admin groups.

mira: I pushed the Role YAML for `deploy-runner` and updated CI to use a namespaced RoleBinding. After we merge we should run `kubectl auth can-i` from the CI pod to validate. Example test:

```
kubectl auth can-i create deployments --as system:serviceaccount:infra:ci-deploy-sa
```

jordan: I'll run the scan across clusters and remove any extra bindings. If we find other SAs with broad perms, will open follow-up tickets.

ops-bot: SECURITY-488 updated: remediation in progress, assigned to alex. Status: in-progress.

sam: Also a note on audit logging — please enable token annotation in the k8s audit policy so we can tie actions back to the CI job id. Otherwise it looks like generic SA activity.

alex: Will enable audit policy change and drop a one-off script to rotate the token and patch KMS IAM. Will post the remediation steps and timeline in the ticket.

mira: Postmortem action: refactor deploy pipeline to use ephemeral credentials + workload identity. Add test in CI that asserts no ClusterRoleBindings exist for infra SAs. Add RBAC linting to PRs.

alex: Quick rollback plan: if PR causes failures, we'll rebind the old ClusterRoleBinding and run a short maintenance window. But let's try to avoid reintroducing cluster-admin. Prefer safe emergency RBAC role with broad but monitored perms instead.

jordan: I'll also check GPU pool node labels — add `rbac.redwood.com/gpu-managed=true` and gate scheduler so only proper nodeSelectors can hit those nodes.

sam: thanks everyone. Assigning follow-ups in SECURITY-488 and PRODUCT-712 (deploy pipeline refactor). :thumbsup:

mira: I'll coordinate with infra on workload identity timeline — aiming for next sprint.
